name: Nexlam-GCN
description: A hybrid graphene and carbon nanotube composite laminate developed by Apex Nanofabrication that exploits the complementary geometries of two-dimensional graphene sheets and one-dimensional CNT fibers to create an isotropically reinforced matrix with no preferred failure plane. CNT fibers are grown directly from graphene sheet edges using a catalytic chemical vapor deposition process, creating covalent bonding between the two carbon allotrope phases rather than simple mechanical mixing. The resulting material combines graphene's in-plane properties with CNT's out-of-plane reinforcement in a single unified composite.
applications: satellite and orbital platform structural members
story_hooks: Nexlam-GCN is appearing in Tier 2 black market fabrication shops in small quantities — someone is either stealing it from orbital manufacturing supply chains or has cracked a partial synthesis route, and the material provenance cannot be traced.

A prosthetics clinic in a Tier 3 district has sourced Nexlam-GCN structural cores for veteran patients at a fraction of market price, raising questions about where the material came from and who is subsidizing it — and why.

The only facility licensed to produce Nexlam-GCN in the region has gone silent, its comms dark and its personnel unaccounted for, leaving several critical aerospace contracts in limbo and competitors circling.
